title: The Salt Monsoon
premise: Rosalind Yarrow, a desert ranger who has spent years erasing himself from every record, is hired to track a thief who stole his late father's brass compass—the one thing he inherited besides debt. His pursuit collides with the disappearance of a government survey team near the drowned city of Vess, where the monsoon floods reveal a wrecked treasure ship for only six tides each season. Rosalind discovers the thief is his estranged half-sister Maren, and that their father was the surveyor who mapped the wreck before dying under suspicious orders from the salvage fleet's magnate, Aldous Crane. Racing Crane's fleet across the salt flats, Rosalind must choose between claiming the inheritance that would restore his name and destroying the survey records that would let power corrupt the drowned city forever; in the end he sinks the evidence, saves Maren, and lets the tide take both the treasure and his claim.
about_author: Felix Brightwater is the pen name of a former hydrographic surveyor who spent a decade mapping coastlines before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels about landscapes that keep secrets, drawing on his obsession with tides, deserts, and the people who vanish into both.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector's Compass
chapters.summary: Rosalind Yarrow's POV. In the border town of Cinder Wells, creditors seize everything Rosalind owns except his ranger kit—until he learns his father's brass compass, left to him in a will he never read, was stolen days ago by a buyer named Salt. The emotional beat: humiliation hardening into purpose; he takes the tracking contract himself.

chapters.title: Tracks on Nothing
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. He reads the thief's trail across the salt pan: careful steps, water discipline, a woman's stride. Flashbacks establish his father's coldness and why Rosalind chose invisibility over inheritance. Emotional beat: reluctant respect for a quarry who moves like family.

chapters.title: The Survey That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. At a waystation he finds the government survey team's abandoned gear—food untouched, instruments running, no tracks leaving. A dying junior surveyor whispers about 'the sixth tide' and a name: Crane. Emotional beat: dread replacing curiosity; this is bigger than theft.

chapters.title: Maren
chapters.summary: Maren's POV, first time. She reveals she lifted the compass deliberately to draw Rosalind out of hiding, knowing he'd track it. She shows him their father's hidden logbook page: coordinates for the wreck of the Meridian, and an accusation against Aldous Crane. Emotional beat: fury at being manipulated, tangled with recognition of kinship.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The monsoon arrives early; the flats begin flooding toward Vess. Maren explains the window: the wreck is reachable for six tides, then sealed for a year. Crane's salvage fleet is two days behind them. Emotional beat: the clock starts—a pact of necessity between strangers who share blood.

chapters.title: The Fleet on the Horizon
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. First sighting of Crane's ships crawling across the flooded pan like beetles. The pair takes a dangerous shortcut through the Needle Rocks; Rosalind nearly drowns saving the compass case. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into competitiveness—he will not let Crane win his father's legacy.

chapters.title: What Father Left
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Around a fire, she shares childhood memories of their father that contradict Rosalind's entirely—one man, two faces. They argue about whether he was a coward or a martyr. Emotional beat: grief surfacing as conflict; the wound beneath the rivalry exposed.

chapters.title: Vess Rising
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. They reach the drowned city at low tide—towers breaching the shallows like ribs. They find the survey team's camp inside a bell tower, signs of a struggle, and a government seal burned off documents. Emotional beat: awe curdling into suspicion; someone wanted this place forgotten.

chapters.title: Crane's Offer
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. An advance boat intercepts them; Crane's lieutenant offers pardons, money, and legitimacy if they hand over the logbook. Rosalind refuses, but the meeting reveals Crane knows about Maren—and about Rosalind's debts. Emotional beat: temptation met and refused, but doubt planted.

chapters.title: The Drowned Archive
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Diving the flooded archive vault, they recover their father's full survey: the Meridian carried not gold but a charter granting mineral rights to whoever holds its papers. Their father hid it to keep it from Crane. Emotional beat: revelation—the treasure is power itself, and inheritance means complicity.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Low Water
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Maren admits she planned to sell the charter to Crane all along—to buy back their family name. Rosalind, betrayed twice by Yarrows, walks out into the rising tide alone. Emotional beat: heartbreak; love against duty splits down bloodlines.

chapters.title: Taken
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Crane's men capture Maren and take the charter. Aboard the flagship she meets Crane, who knew her father—and confesses he ordered the survey team silenced. Emotional beat: Maren realizes her bargain was always a trap; the corrupter corrupts what he touches.

chapters.title: The Third Tide
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Alone, half-drowned, Rosalind rallies stranded survey-team survivors hiding in Vess who distrust Crane. Together they plan to board the flagship during the third tide using the flooded streets as cover. Emotional beat: isolation ending; the invisible man chooses allies.

chapters.title: Boarding the Meridian's Ghost
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The infiltration begins—swimming the submerged causeway, cutting the fleet's anchor lines. A survivor sacrifices herself to hold a hatch against guards. Emotional beat: cost made real; heroism measured in losses, not glory.

chapters.title: Father's Last Tide
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Imprisoned, Maren finds Crane's private papers proving their father died sabotaging Crane's first salvage attempt—not fleeing debt as Rosalind believed. She resolves to tell him, whatever it costs. Emotional beat: the dead father redeemed; truth as inheritance.

chapters.title: Reunion Under Guns
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind reaches the brig during the fourth tide; siblings reunite mid-escape, exchanging truths—his shame, her betrayal, their father's sacrifice. Crane springs the trap, sealing them in the flooding hold. Emotional beat: reconciliation forged under mortal pressure.

chapters.title: The Fifth Tide
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Escape through the drowning hold as the sea reclaims the ship's lower decks; Rosalind nearly dies holding the escape valve for Maren and the survivors. Emotional beat: selflessness completing his arc—the man who hoarded nothing finally gives everything.

chapters.title: Crane's Court
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Cornered on deck, they face Crane, who offers Rosalind the one thing he wants: legitimacy, his name restored, the debt erased—in exchange for the charter. Rosalind looks at Maren, at the survivors, at the sea. Emotional beat: the final temptation, duty versus desire laid bare.

chapters.title: Sinking the Charter
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind burns the charter and drops the ashes into the sixth tide, declaring the wreck belongs to no one. Crane's crew, learning he murdered the surveyors, mutinies. Emotional beat: climax—power renounced, corruption collapsing under its own weight.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Water
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The fleet scatters; Crane escapes in a longboat, diminished but alive—a thread of consequence. The survivors claim Vess as common ground, not property. Maren and Rosalind stand on the tower at sunset, orphans of the same father at last at peace. Emotional beat: exhaustion and quiet wonder.

chapters.title: The Compass Returned
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Back in Cinder Wells, creditors come for the last of nothing and find a man with no debt and no treasure, content. He gives Maren the compass—she'll chart honest maps now—and keeps only the tracking contract. Emotional beat: resolution; inheritance redefined as what you carry forward, not what you own.

chapters.title: Monsoon Season
chapters.summary: Dual POV, alternating. One year later: the monsoon rises again over Vess, now a free settlement. Rosalind rangers the flats; Maren surveys openly. A letter arrives hinting Crane survived and remembers. They look at the water together. Emotional beat: earned peace shadowed by sequel-ready possibility—love and duty finally pointing the same direction.
